events.continuity_hook: Adds a final practical timing check to the Boise utility pilot-acceptance trip after the booking is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Update the concise Boise itinerary with the revised gate, PPE, debrief, hotel, rental-car, and airport timing while leaving the booked reservations unchanged.
events.scenario_brief: The Boise trip is already booked, but the utility sends a visitor packet with a different gate, a stricter PPE check-in time, and a Friday operator debrief moved earlier in the morning. Jonah does not want to revisit the flights, rental car, or Meridian hotel; he only needs the arrival-night drive plan, hotel parking note, Thursday site arrival buffer, Friday checkout timing, and return-airport timing tightened around the new plant access instructions.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new distributor and food-plant trip after the Boise site visit logistics are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Create a flight, hotel, and rental-car shortlist that protects the Tuesday training and Wednesday plant access window while keeping the return date flexible.
events.scenario_brief: A Twin Cities distributor asks Jonah to run a Tuesday lunch-and-learn and then join a Wednesday morning CIP skid review at a food-and-beverage plant south of Minneapolis. He needs Bay Area-to-MSP flight options for a Monday afternoon departure, with clean routing more important than carrier if the nonstop choices are limited. Hotels should compare an airport-area option with easier highway access against a higher-rated Bloomington or Eagan property with better dinner choices. The unresolved items are whether the plant wants a late-Wednesday validation readout and whether the demo sample case arrives before he does.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Twin Cities planning after equipment logistics and the plant access time become firmer.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the outbound flight, hotel location, rental-car timing, and likely return window around the expanded Tuesday agenda and early Wednesday plant start.
events.scenario_brief: The distributor confirms the demo case will be at the branch Monday morning, and the plant locks a 7:00 a.m. Wednesday escort time. The Tuesday session also expands to include a short morning calibration review before the lunch-and-learn. Jonah wants to narrow the travel plan between a better-timed SFO-to-MSP nonstop and a lower-cost Oakland one-stop that arrives later, then compare the airport hotel against a higher-rated Eagan property with easier evening meals and a shorter Wednesday drive. The return is still unresolved because the plant may ask for an end-of-day validation readout.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Twin Cities distributor and food-plant trip from comparison to booking once the validation schedule is settled.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, rental car, hotel reservation, room request, seat selections, and compact agenda for the distributor training and plant review.
events.scenario_brief: The plant asks Jonah to stay through Wednesday afternoon for the validation readout, so he chooses a Thursday midday return rather than a rushed Wednesday evening departure. He books the Monday afternoon SFO-to-MSP nonstop, a compact rental car, and the higher-rated Eagan hotel because it shortens the Wednesday drive while still offering nearby restaurants and reliable parking. The room note should request a coffee maker and mini-fridge, and window seats should be selected where available.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new utility controls-workshop trip after the Twin Cities booking is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight, hotel, and rental-car shortlist that protects the Tuesday workshop while showing the trade-off between the nonstop flight, connecting options, hotel location, and possible Thursday stay.
events.scenario_brief: A Carolina municipal utility asks Jonah to lead a controls workshop on Tuesday and attend a Wednesday site walk-through at a nearby treatment plant. He needs Bay Area-to-Charlotte flight options for a Monday departure that allow time for a rental-car pickup and slide review that evening. The best-looking nonstop is not on his usual favored carrier, while the preferred-carrier choices involve connections that could create timing risk. Hotels should compare an airport-adjacent property with simpler driving against an uptown option with stronger restaurants and guest feedback. The unresolved items are whether a distributor dinner lands Tuesday night and whether a procurement meeting will be added Thursday morning.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Carolina utility planning after the extra meeting and distributor dinner are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the flight, hotel location, rental-car timing, and Thursday return window around the workshop, dinner, plant walk-through, and procurement meeting.
events.scenario_brief: The utility adds a Thursday morning procurement meeting, making a Wednesday return impractical, and the distributor dinner is confirmed for Tuesday near uptown Charlotte. Jonah wants to narrow the outbound flight between the Monday afternoon nonstop and a one-stop itinerary that is cheaper but less predictable. For hotels, he is now weighing the uptown property near the dinner against a better-driving airport-area hotel for the plant visit. The remaining open item is whether the Thursday return should be midafternoon or early evening after the procurement meeting.
